decisions.reason: The rejected bit-time claim is overstrong: eta=(2^m+1)/(4*2^m) is reduced, stays near 1/4, and has unbounded binary numerator/denominator length while 1/eta remains bounded. The stated procedure parses eta and computes rational mesh sizes and compiler tolerances; this work is not bounded by a polynomial in the matrix-description length and 1/eta alone. The actual Solovay–Kitaev Statement explicitly charges s_epsilon. This is a logic defect in the resource inference of step 4.1, rather than a missing dependency. Repaired the Statement to charge b+ell(eta)+1/eta in bit time, clarified F3, and proved the parsing and derived-tolerance bounds in step 4.1; the gate-count bound and synthesis guarantee are preserved.

The corrected bit-time bound includes the exact rational tolerance encoding, with fixed-dimension query arithmetic and compiler calls polynomial in b+ell(eta)+1/eta; the fixed number of compiled factors retains gate count polynomial in b+1/eta. This is adjudication with a local repair, not independent review of that repair.
